report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Fixed deadline (6 months) with one developer covering PM/design/dev roles creates execution uncertainty; scope is large (Zendesk replacement) with evolving stakeholder needs; team lacks dedicated PM and design capacity to lock requirements upfront.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Build a comprehensive internal IT service desk system to replace manual ticket handling with self-service, automated routing, SLA tracking, and dashboards.
project_understanding.beneficiary: IT team (5 people) and all employees (500 users); IT manager for visibility and SLA management.
project_understanding.trigger: IT team is drowning in manual ticket processing with no visibility into workload or SLA compliance; need to reduce operational burden and improve service transparency.
supporting_quotes: IT is drowning in tickets. Manual processes. No visibility into IT workload or SLAs.
This is essentially replacing Zendesk with a custom solution - typically a 6-month team effort.
Only one developer available - they will do development, PM, and design

assumption_log.what: One developer can deliver PM, design, and full-stack development simultaneously across a 6-month Zendesk-replacement project.
assumption_log.why: Input explicitly states one person will cover all three roles; assumption documents the staffing constraint as a planning baseline.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.2 (Resource Management) — resource constraints must be documented before schedule baseline is set.
assumption_log.consequence: Developer context-switches between PM decisions, design work, and coding; critical path tasks slip; no one owns scope/stakeholder management; burnout and quality degradation.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: plan proceeds with stated constraint. Risks: one person cannot sustain three full-time roles for 26 weeks; project will miss deadline or scope will be cut mid-stream.

assumption_log.what: Mobile app (iOS/Android React Native) is in scope for the 6-month deadline with one developer.
assumption_log.why: Input lists 'Mobile app (iOS/Android)' as a requirement and does not mark it as deferred or phase-2; assumption treats it as MVP scope.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 (Scope Baseline) — scope baseline must be explicit before decomposition.
assumption_log.consequence: Mobile development adds 6-8 weeks of effort (testing, platform-specific bugs, app store submission); timeline becomes impossible; scope must be cut or deadline missed.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: clarifies what 'in scope' means for planning. Risks: if mobile is actually deferred, plan is wrong; if it stays in scope, deadline is unachievable.

assumption_log.what: Integration with 10+ internal systems is achievable within Phase 3 (Integration & Edge Cases) with one developer.
assumption_log.why: Input states 'Must integrate with 10+ internal systems' and 'Integration with Slack for notifications' and 'Email integration'; assumption treats these as parallel integrations, not sequential blockers.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 (Risk Identification) — external dependencies must be identified before schedule is locked.
assumption_log.consequence: Each integration requires API documentation review, sandbox testing, error handling, and monitoring setup; 10+ integrations = 40-60 hours each = 400-600 hours; one developer cannot complete in 4-5 weeks (Phase 3 duration).
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: documents the integration load as a planning assumption. Risks: if integrations are sequential or require external team coordination, Phase 3 becomes 12+ weeks.

assumption_log.what: 99.9% uptime requirement is achievable with one developer and no dedicated DevOps/SRE role.
assumption_log.why: Input specifies 'Must have 99.9% uptime' but does not allocate DevOps capacity; assumption treats uptime as a design/architecture goal, not a staffing gap.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 (Quality Management) — quality metrics must be defined before execution; uptime is a non-functional requirement.
assumption_log.consequence: 99.9% uptime requires redundancy, monitoring, alerting, automated failover, and on-call support; one developer cannot design, build, and operate this; will require DevOps hire or outsourcing.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: documents uptime as a known NFR. Risks: if uptime is truly required, staffing plan is incomplete; if it is aspirational, it should be marked as phase-2 or deferred.

assumption_log.what: Knowledge base, asset management, service catalog, and SLA management are all MVP features (not deferred to phase 2).
assumption_log.why: Input lists all as requirements without marking any as 'nice to have' or 'phase 2'; assumption treats them as in-scope for the 6-month deadline.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 (Scope Baseline) — scope must be explicit and agreed before planning.
assumption_log.consequence: Each feature adds 2-4 weeks of development; knowledge base alone = 3-4 weeks (article creation, search, tagging); asset management = 2-3 weeks; service catalog = 2-3 weeks; total = 7-10 weeks of additional effort beyond core ticket system.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: clarifies MVP scope. Risks: if any feature is deferred, plan is wrong; if all are in scope, timeline is impossible.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: One developer on critical path for all 26 weeks with zero slack; any illness, context-switch, or technical blocker causes immediate deadline slip; no capacity for PM/design decisions or stakeholder management.

phases.name: Discovery & Design
milestones: Requirements document finalized and signed off by IT manager
System architecture approved (ticket flow, integrations, data model)
UI/UX wireframes for core flows (ticket creation, dashboard, mobile)
Integration points mapped (Slack, email, 10+ internal systems)

tasks.name: Conduct IT team interviews and document current ticket workflow
tasks.definition_of_done: Current-state workflow documented; pain points and success metrics agreed with IT manager in writing.

tasks.name: Design system architecture (ticket routing, SLA engine, notification system)
tasks.definition_of_done: Architecture diagram approved; database schema drafted; integration points identified for all 10+ systems.

tasks.name: Create UI/UX wireframes for ticket creation, dashboard, mobile app
tasks.definition_of_done: Wireframes for 8+ core screens approved by IT manager; mobile-first design confirmed.

tasks.name: Document integration requirements for Slack, email, and internal systems
tasks.definition_of_done: API documentation reviewed for all 10+ systems; sandbox access confirmed; authentication strategy documented.

tasks.name: Finalize requirements document and obtain stakeholder sign-off
tasks.definition_of_done: Requirements document signed by IT manager and executive sponsor; scope locked; change control process agreed.

phases.name: Core Development
milestones: Ticket creation and management API complete
Internal demo with IT team (core flows only)

tasks.name: Set up Django project, PostgreSQL database, and CI/CD pipeline
tasks.definition_of_done: Django project scaffolded; PostgreSQL running locally and in staging; GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline passing.

tasks.name: Design and implement PostgreSQL schema for tickets, users, assets, SLAs
tasks.definition_of_done: Schema supports ticket CRUD, user roles, asset tracking, SLA definitions; migrations tested; indexes added for performance.

tasks.name: Implement ticket creation and management API endpoints
tasks.definition_of_done: POST /tickets, GET /tickets, PATCH /tickets/{id}, DELETE /tickets/{id} endpoints working; authentication and authorization enforced.

tasks.name: Implement SLA engine (calculate breach time, trigger alerts)
tasks.definition_of_done: SLA rules engine calculates breach time; alerts triggered 1 hour before breach; SLA metrics queryable via API.

tasks.name: Build React frontend for ticket creation and list views
tasks.definition_of_done: Ticket creation form functional; ticket list with filtering and sorting; responsive design; form validation working.

tasks.name: Implement dashboard backend (ticket counts, SLA metrics, queue depth)
tasks.definition_of_done: Dashboard API endpoints return ticket counts, SLA breach %, queue depth, agent utilization; data aggregation tested.

tasks.name: Build React dashboard UI for IT manager
tasks.definition_of_done: Dashboard displays ticket counts, SLA metrics, queue depth, agent performance; charts render correctly; data refreshes every 5 minutes.

tasks.name: Implement knowledge base article CRUD and search
tasks.definition_of_done: Articles can be created, edited, deleted; full-text search working; articles tagged and categorized.

tasks.name: Build knowledge base UI (article list, search, detail view)
tasks.definition_of_done: Article search functional; detail view renders markdown; related articles suggested; mobile-responsive.

tasks.name: Implement automated ticket routing logic (assign to queue based on category)
tasks.definition_of_done: Tickets automatically routed to correct queue; routing rules configurable; audit trail of routing decisions.

phases.name: Integration & Edge Cases
milestones: Email integration working (ticket creation from email)

tasks.name: Implement Slack API integration for ticket notifications
tasks.definition_of_done: Slack messages sent on ticket creation, assignment, and closure; message formatting correct; error handling for Slack API failures.

tasks.name: Implement email integration (SendGrid) for ticket creation and updates
tasks.definition_of_done: Emails trigger ticket creation; ticket updates sent via email; reply-to-email creates comments; email parsing handles attachments.

tasks.name: Build asset management module (track laptops, equipment, licenses)
tasks.definition_of_done: Asset CRUD endpoints; asset assignment to users; deprecation tracking; audit trail of asset changes.

tasks.name: Build asset management UI (list, detail, assignment)
tasks.definition_of_done: Asset list with filtering; detail view shows assignment history; bulk assignment UI; mobile-responsive.

tasks.name: Build service catalog module (request software, equipment, services)
tasks.definition_of_done: Service catalog CRUD; request workflow (submit, approve, fulfill); approval routing; request status tracking.

tasks.name: Build service catalog UI (browse, request, track)
tasks.definition_of_done: Service catalog browsable; request form functional; request tracking page shows status; approval notifications sent.

tasks.name: Integrate with 10+ internal systems (LDAP, HR system, asset DB, etc.)
tasks.definition_of_done: All 10+ integrations tested in sandbox; data mapping validated; error handling for API failures; monitoring alerts configured.

tasks.name: Implement user satisfaction rating system (post-ticket survey)
tasks.definition_of_done: Survey sent after ticket closure; ratings stored; satisfaction metrics queryable; dashboard shows satisfaction trend.

tasks.name: Conduct security review and implement authentication/authorization
tasks.definition_of_done: Security review completed; OAuth/SSO implemented; role-based access control enforced; SQL injection and XSS mitigated; HTTPS enforced.

phases.name: QA & Testing
milestones: Performance testing at 500 concurrent users completed
UAT with IT team completed and signed off

tasks.name: Develop comprehensive test suite (unit, integration, end-to-end)
tasks.definition_of_done: Test coverage > 80% for critical paths; all integration tests passing; end-to-end tests for ticket workflow, SLA, routing.

tasks.name: Execute performance testing (500 concurrent users, response time < 2s)
tasks.definition_of_done: Load test results show < 2s response time at 500 concurrent users; database queries optimized; caching strategy validated.

tasks.name: Build and test React Native mobile app (iOS/Android)
tasks.definition_of_done: Mobile app builds for iOS and Android; core flows (ticket creation, list, detail) working; tested on physical devices; app store submission ready.

tasks.name: Conduct UAT with IT team (5 users, 2-week period)
tasks.definition_of_done: IT team completes UAT checklist; critical bugs fixed; sign-off document signed by IT manager; feedback incorporated.

tasks.name: Perform accessibility audit (WCAG 2.1 AA compliance)
tasks.definition_of_done: Accessibility audit completed; WCAG 2.1 AA compliance verified; color contrast, keyboard navigation, screen reader support confirmed.

tasks.name: Execute load testing for 99.9% uptime (failover, redundancy validation)
tasks.definition_of_done: Load test shows 99.9% uptime achievable; failover tested; database replication working; monitoring alerts validated.

tasks.name: Fix critical and high-priority bugs identified in testing
tasks.definition_of_done: All critical bugs resolved; high-priority bugs fixed; regression testing passed; bug tracking system cleared of blockers.

tasks.name: Deploy to production (database migration, DNS cutover, smoke tests)
tasks.definition_of_done: Production deployment completed; smoke tests passing; rollback plan tested; monitoring alerts firing correctly.

tasks.name: Configure monitoring, alerting, and logging (uptime, performance, errors)
tasks.definition_of_done: Monitoring dashboard live; alerts configured for uptime, response time, error rate; log aggregation working; on-call runbook ready.

tasks.name: Write system documentation, runbooks, and troubleshooting guides
tasks.definition_of_done: System architecture documented; runbooks for common operations (backup, restore, scaling); troubleshooting guide for IT team.

tasks.name: Conduct IT team training (system usage, administration, troubleshooting)
tasks.definition_of_done: IT team trained on system usage, admin functions, and troubleshooting; training materials provided; Q&A session completed.

tasks.name: Obtain go-live sign-off from IT manager and executive sponsor
tasks.definition_of_done: Go-live sign-off document signed; IT manager confirms readiness; system live for all 500 employees.

risk_register.description: One developer cannot simultaneously perform PM, design, and full-stack development for a Zendesk-replacement project; context-switching will cause critical path delays and quality degradation.
risk_register.trigger: Developer reports context-switching overhead; PM decisions delayed; design reviews blocked; code quality issues emerge.
risk_register.mitigation: Hire or allocate a dedicated PM and UX designer immediately (before Phase 2 starts); reduce developer scope to coding only; establish decision-making authority for PM role.
risk_register.contingency: If PM/design resources unavailable, cut scope to core ticket system only (remove knowledge base, asset management, service catalog, mobile app); extend timeline to 9 months.

risk_register.description: Mobile app (iOS/Android React Native) adds 6-8 weeks of development, testing, and app store submission; one developer cannot deliver mobile + web + integrations in 6 months.
risk_register.trigger: Mobile development begins in Phase 2; developer realizes platform-specific bugs, testing overhead, and app store submission delays.
risk_register.mitigation: Defer mobile app to phase 2 (post-launch); deliver web-only MVP in 6 months; mobile follows in months 7-9.
risk_register.contingency: If mobile is required for launch, cut knowledge base, asset management, and service catalog from MVP; deliver mobile + core ticket system only.

risk_register.description: 10+ internal system integrations require API documentation review, sandbox testing, error handling, and monitoring; one developer cannot complete 40-60 hours per integration in Phase 3 (5.5 weeks).
risk_register.trigger: Phase 3 begins; developer discovers API documentation gaps, sandbox access delays, or undocumented API behavior; integration testing reveals data mapping issues.
risk_register.mitigation: Prioritize integrations by business value; deliver 3-4 critical integrations in MVP (Slack, email, LDAP, HR system); defer remaining 6+ to phase 2.
risk_register.contingency: If all 10+ integrations required for launch, extend Phase 3 to 10-12 weeks; compress Phase 4 (QA) to 3 weeks; accept higher risk of bugs in production.

risk_register.description: 99.9% uptime requirement (52.6 minutes downtime per year) requires redundancy, automated failover, monitoring, alerting, and on-call support; one developer cannot design and operate this without DevOps/SRE role.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 5 deployment; system experiences downtime due to single points of failure; monitoring gaps prevent rapid incident response.
risk_register.mitigation: Hire or allocate a dedicated DevOps/SRE engineer before Phase 3; design for high availability (database replication, load balancing, automated failover); implement comprehensive monitoring.
risk_register.contingency: If DevOps unavailable, reduce uptime target to 99.5% (3.7 hours downtime per year); accept manual failover and longer incident response times; document operational limitations.

risk_register.description: Knowledge base, asset management, service catalog, and SLA management are all listed as MVP requirements; together they add 7-10 weeks of development beyond core ticket system.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 development; developer realizes feature scope exceeds available time; stakeholder pressure to deliver all features by deadline.
risk_register.mitigation: Obtain written scope sign-off from IT manager and executive sponsor; define MVP as core ticket system + dashboard + SLA tracking only; defer knowledge base, asset management, and service catalog to phase 2.
risk_register.contingency: If all features required for launch, extend timeline to 9-12 months; hire additional developers (2-3 more); accept higher budget and schedule risk.

risk_register.description: One developer allocated at 100% for 26 weeks with zero slack on critical path; any illness, vacation, or technical blocker causes immediate deadline slip.
risk_register.trigger: Developer takes vacation, becomes ill, or encounters unexpected technical blocker (e.g., database performance issue, API integration failure).
risk_register.mitigation: Hire a backup developer (junior or mid-level) to shadow critical path tasks; cross-train on architecture and key modules; establish knowledge transfer plan.
risk_register.contingency: If backup unavailable, extend timeline by 2-4 weeks to account for single-person risk; document all critical decisions and code in detail for knowledge transfer.

risk_register.description: 6-month deadline for a Zendesk-replacement project with one developer is aggressive; typical team effort is 6 months with 3-4 developers.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 development; developer realizes velocity is lower than estimated; critical path tasks slip by 1-2 weeks.
risk_register.mitigation: Reduce scope to MVP (core ticket system + dashboard + SLA tracking); defer mobile app, knowledge base, asset management, and service catalog to phase 2.
risk_register.contingency: If scope cannot be reduced, extend timeline to 9 months; hire 1-2 additional developers; accept higher budget.

risk_register.description: System handles employee data (tickets, assets, requests) and must meet security and compliance requirements (authentication, authorization, audit trail, data retention); security review not scoped in Phase 3.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 3 security review; compliance gaps identified (missing encryption, weak authentication, no audit trail); remediation requires 2-3 weeks of rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Allocate security engineer for Phase 3 security review; implement OAuth/SSO, role-based access control, and audit logging from Phase 2; conduct security review before Phase 4.
risk_register.contingency: If security gaps discovered late, extend Phase 4 by 2-3 weeks; defer non-critical security features to phase 2; accept higher risk of compliance violations.

risk_register.description: React Native mobile app development requires platform-specific testing (iOS/Android), device testing, and app store submission; one developer cannot deliver quality mobile app in 4 weeks (Phase 4).
risk_register.trigger: Phase 4 mobile testing; platform-specific bugs emerge (iOS/Android differences); app store submission rejected due to policy violations.
risk_register.mitigation: Defer mobile app to phase 2; hire mobile developer if mobile is required for launch; allocate 8-10 weeks for mobile development, testing, and app store submission.
risk_register.contingency: If mobile required for launch, extend Phase 4 to 6-7 weeks; accept higher risk of bugs and app store rejection; plan for rapid iteration post-launch.

risk_register.description: Email integration (SendGrid) for ticket creation requires email parsing, attachment handling, and reply-to-email workflow; complexity underestimated in Phase 3.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 3 email integration; developer discovers email parsing edge cases (forwarded emails, quoted text, attachments); implementation takes 3-4 weeks instead of 2.
risk_register.mitigation: Use email parsing library (e.g., email-reply-parser); implement comprehensive email handling tests; allocate 3-4 weeks for email integration instead of 2.
risk_register.contingency: If email integration delayed, defer to phase 2; deliver Slack + web UI for ticket creation in MVP; email integration follows post-launch.

risk_register.description: Stakeholder expectations for a Zendesk replacement may exceed MVP scope; IT manager may expect all features (knowledge base, asset management, service catalog, mobile app) in 6 months.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 requirements review; IT manager requests all features in MVP; scope creep pressure increases as deadline approaches.
risk_register.mitigation: Obtain written scope sign-off from IT manager and executive sponsor in Phase 1; define MVP clearly; establish change control process; communicate scope trade-offs upfront.
risk_register.contingency: If scope creep occurs, extend timeline or reduce features; document all scope changes and impact on deadline; obtain re-approval from stakeholders.

risk_register.description: No QA engineer allocated; QA effort is 25% of development effort (estimated 280+ hours); one developer cannot perform development and QA simultaneously.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 4 QA; developer realizes testing effort exceeds available time; critical bugs slip to production.
risk_register.mitigation: Hire or allocate a dedicated QA engineer for Phases 3-4; establish test automation framework in Phase 2; allocate 25% of development hours to QA.
risk_register.contingency: If QA unavailable, extend Phase 4 to 6-7 weeks; accept higher risk of bugs in production; plan for rapid iteration post-launch.

open_questions.question: Is the one-person team (PM + design + development) confirmed as the only available resource, or can dedicated PM and UX designer be allocated before Phase 2 starts?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If one person must cover all three roles, project will miss deadline or scope will be cut mid-stream; critical path has zero slack and context-switching will cause delays.

open_questions.question: Is the mobile app (iOS/Android React Native) truly required for the 6-month MVP launch, or can it be deferred to phase 2 (post-launch)?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Mobile app adds 6-8 weeks of development and testing; if required for launch, timeline becomes impossible with one developer; if deferred, scope is achievable.

open_questions.question: Which of the 10+ internal system integrations are critical for MVP launch, and which can be deferred to phase 2?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Phase 3 integration work (60 hours) is underestimated for 10+ systems; prioritization will determine whether MVP is achievable in 6 months.

open_questions.question: Can a dedicated QA engineer and DevOps engineer be allocated for Phases 3-5, or will one developer perform all testing and deployment?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: QA and DevOps are under-allocated; if unavailable, testing and deployment quality will suffer; 99.9% uptime requirement cannot be met without DevOps expertise.

open_questions.question: Has the IT manager formally signed off on the MVP scope (core ticket system + dashboard + SLA tracking), or are all features (knowledge base, asset management, service catalog, mobile app) expected in the 6-month launch?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Scope creep is the highest risk; if all features are expected, timeline is impossible; written scope sign-off is required before Phase 2 starts.

pm_confidence_score.interpretation: PM confidence score is 28.0 because the project has six CRITICAL risks (one-person team, mobile app scope, integration complexity, uptime requirements, feature scope, and single point of failure), five HIGH risks, and five major assumptions that are unsustainable for a 26-week Zendesk replacement. The project is NOT VIABLE as currently scoped with the stated constraints.

project_viability.gap_amount: One developer cannot deliver Zendesk replacement in 6 months; estimated effort is 1,200+ hours (3-4 developers × 6 months); timeline requires 9-12 months with current team or 3-4 additional developers.

scoping_options.description: Reduce MVP to core ticket system only (ticket creation, list, detail, assignment, SLA tracking, dashboard). Defer knowledge base, asset management, service catalog, and mobile app to phase 2 (post-launch).
scoping_options.impact: Delivers core ticket system in 6 months with one developer; addresses primary pain point (manual ticket handling); enables phased rollout.
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Knowledge base, asset management, and service catalog deferred 3-6 months; mobile app deferred 3-6 months; IT team must use web-only interface initially; some stakeholder expectations unmet at launch.

scoping_options.description: Hire 2-3 additional developers (mid-level or senior) to parallelize work; allocate dedicated PM and UX designer; hire QA engineer and DevOps engineer. Deliver full scope in 6 months with 5-6 person team.
scoping_options.impact: Full scope delivered in 6 months; all features (knowledge base, asset management, service catalog, mobile app) available at launch; higher quality and test coverage.
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Budget increases from $100K to $250K-$350K (additional salaries, contractors); hiring timeline may delay start; team coordination overhead increases; risk of onboarding delays.

scoping_options.description: Extend timeline to 9-12 months with one developer; hire dedicated PM, UX designer, QA engineer, and DevOps engineer (phased hiring). Deliver full scope in phases (core ticket system in 6 months, mobile app in 9 months, advanced features in 12 months).
scoping_options.impact: Full scope delivered over 12 months; phased rollout reduces risk; team grows gradually; quality improves with dedicated roles.
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Misses 6-month deadline; IT team continues manual processes for 6+ months; budget increases to $150K-$200K; stakeholder expectations may not align with phased delivery.
